sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source includes the Saluzzo-Sommariva di Bosco blind thrust system which runs in the southern Piemonte plain. This is composed of a system of NE-SW trending, N-verging blind thrusts and it was mapped using subsurface geological and geophysical data that show that these tectonic structures bound to the north the so called Savigliano basin and deform the plio-Quaternary stratigraphic sequence.
In contrast with the geological evidence of recent activity, the Italian historical and instrumental catalogues show few moderate earthquakes that hit the southern Piemonte region, mostly concentrated near the foothills of the Western Alps. In the broad Piemonte region, the largest events occurred south-west of Torino at the Alps foothills during a seismic sequence which included two shocks of Mw 5.6 and Mw 5.3 on the 2 and 16 April 1808 (CPTI15; Rovida et al., 2016).
The outermost Apennine thrust fronts are traditionally divided into three arcs, that from west to east are: the Monferrato, the Emilia, and the Ferrara-Romagna arcs. In the central and eastern sectors (i.e. Emilia and Ferrara-Romagna arcs) they are buried below the sediments of the Po Plain and have been mapped using subsurface geophysical exploration data. These structures deform the base of the Plio-Quaternary sequence south of the Po River, and are formed by blind, north-verging thrusts and folds. Conversely, the north-verging Monferrato Arc, that is the westernmost of the three Northern Apennines arcs, is an outcropping anticlinorium. The Saluzzo-Sommariva di Bosco blind thrust system runs south of the Monferrato Arc and in this respect may represent an out-of-sequence structure of the Northern Apennines belt.
The strike of this Source was taken from the general orientation of the tectonic structures mapped using subsurface data. The dip was inferred from geological cross-sections and the shape of the thrust related anticline. The rake was assumed to represent thrusting based on general geodynamic considerations. The minimum and maximum depths were inferred by geometrical considerations concerning the depth at which active thrusting is rooted. The slip rate was inferred from regional geodynamic data.

pictures.c: Map showing the western continuation of the Collina Torinese thrust, buried in the plain between Torino and Pinerolo (from Collo [1995]). This structure links the uplifted western tip of the Monferrato with the foothills of the western Alps. The activity of the westernmost section of this blind thrust front is testified by the uplift of middle Pleistocene fluvial deposits cropping out ENE of Pinerolo in the "Rilievo di Riva" (marked by an X in figure).
